name: FRED-MD archival next-month CPI and unemployment

license.terms: BLS public-domain series, citation requested. Scope limited to CPIAUCSL and UNRATE.

source_citation: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPIAUCSL and UNRATE, via FRED and FRED-MD, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, October 2026 vintage.

cpiaucsl.target_name: US all-items consumer price index, seasonally adjusted
cpiaucsl.instruction: Estimate the US all-items consumer price index, seasonally adjusted for the month following the history.
cpiaucsl.field_description: The two arrays contain 24 consecutive US monthly observations, oldest to newest. CPIAUCSL is the seasonally adjusted all-items CPI (1982-1984=100). UNRATE is the seasonally adjusted civilian unemployment rate in percent. first_month dates the first observation. Data use the October 2026 vintage.

unrate.target_name: US civilian unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted
unrate.instruction: Estimate the US civilian unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted for the month following the history.
unrate.field_description: The two arrays contain 24 consecutive US monthly observations, oldest to newest. CPIAUCSL is the seasonally adjusted all-items CPI (1982-1984=100). UNRATE is the seasonally adjusted civilian unemployment rate in percent. first_month dates the first observation. Data use the October 2026 vintage.

preparation: Revised-history task. Input ends one calendar month before target. The first 24 months provide history only. Missing input cells remain null. References count the Transform: line as CSV data row 1.
split_guidance: Split both tasks by target month together. Account for overlapping windows. This snapshot contains later revisions and does not support real-time forecasting claims.

stats.name: FRED-MD archival next-month CPI and unemployment

deduplication_rule: Same task, normalized input, normalized label AND official split; preserve all source_refs. Across-split copies retained and flagged, same-input dependencies unioned. Different labels retained.
sample_id_rule: sha256([task_id,input_hash,label,split]) first 24 hex; official split included to preserve split occurrences.
